name: Quarterly earnings summary (faithful)
question: Can you summarise Corvane Systems' third-quarter fiscal 2026 results for me, including growth, margins, guidance and anything notable from the investor call?
description: A faithful paraphrase of an earnings release and call summary, including details that only the second source contains.
response: Corvane Systems brought in $412 million in revenue in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, a 14 percent increase over the same period last year. Gross margin widened to 46.2 percent from 43.8 percent a year ago, which CFO Desmond Okafor attributed mainly to cheaper components and a more favourable product mix. Operating income came in at $58 million, or about 14.1 percent of revenue. The company lifted its full-year revenue outlook to a range of $1.62 billion to $1.65 billion. On the call, management said the Halden vibration monitors now make up roughly a third of sales, and Asia-Pacific revenue rose 22 percent while Europe was flat. Corvane finished the quarter with 3,870 employees and does not expect to add staff in the fourth quarter beyond backfilling departures.

sources.title: Corvane Systems reports third-quarter fiscal 2026 results
sources.text: Corvane Systems, a maker of industrial sensing equipment based in Tillbury, reported revenue of $412 million for the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Revenue grew 14 percent compared with the same quarter a year earlier, driven mainly by demand for its Halden line of vibration monitors. Gross margin was 46.2 percent, up from 43.8 percent in the prior-year quarter. Operating income rose to $58 million, giving an operating margin of 14.1 percent. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to between $1.62 billion and $1.65 billion. Chief Executive Officer Marisol Atwater said the quarter showed that customers are willing to pay for reliability. Corvane ended the quarter with 3,870 employees.

sources.title: Corvane Systems Q3 fiscal 2026 investor call summary
sources.text: During the investor call, Chief Financial Officer Desmond Okafor said the gross margin improvement came mostly from lower component costs and a richer product mix. Okafor noted that the company does not plan to increase headcount in the fourth quarter, apart from replacing employees who leave. Sales in the Asia-Pacific region grew 22 percent, while European sales were flat. Atwater told analysts that Halden monitors now account for roughly one third of total revenue. The company expects fourth-quarter gross margin to be slightly lower than in the third quarter because of a planned retooling at its Brenmoor plant. Okafor said Corvane repurchased $25 million of its shares during the quarter. Management declined to provide guidance for fiscal 2027.
